intro: These reference threads calibrate scores for a comedy podcast built from real Nextdoor drama. Anchor relative levels like this: drama is real conflict, stakes, or escalation—not just loud typing. absurdity is how unhinged or “peak Nextdoor” the situation and voice feel. discussion_spark is how much neighbors would argue, pile on, or riff in the thread. news_value is whether something concrete happened worth reporting (crime, policy, incident). emotional_intensity is heat in the writing (caps, outrage, shock). readability is how tellable the post is aloud (short, clear beats rambling). podcast_worthy is holistic: strong segments usually combine a sharp hook with drama and/or absurdity and good pacing—serious stories can still score high if they drive a compelling segment. Match the shape of these examples when you score new posts; do not copy numbers blindly if the new thread is clearly milder or wilder.

ideal.summary: Author admits a tow-worthy parking mistake, then finds their new leased car keyed, tire stabbed, and graffitied at the impound lot—neighbors debate Seattle reactions and class cues in the alley.
ideal.why_podcast_worthy: Great segment fuel: relatable mistake collides with disproportionate neighbor vigilantism and a long thread of takes.

ideal.summary: All-caps warning about a peeper at the window; author describes confronting someone in the hedges with provocative, chaotic wording and neighbors argue about police and safety.
ideal.why_podcast_worthy: Peak Nextdoor voice and escalation—dark, absurd, and comment-thread gasoline.

ideal.summary: Author reports being assaulted outside a Rainier Lowe’s after staff said there was no parking-lot security; SPD allegedly labeled it mutual combat, sparking a heated thread about policy and blame.
ideal.why_podcast_worthy: Serious incident with a clear narrative hook and huge debate energy—strong show material despite the heavy topic.

ideal.summary: Detailed account of indecent exposure in a Target women’s restroom, store response, and follow-up reporting; comments explode over corporate policy and child safety.
ideal.why_podcast_worthy: Long-form, high-stakes retail-neighborhood story with policy angle—heavy, but very discussable on-mic with care.

ideal.summary: Short outrage post: neighbor urinated in their own driveway in view of the porch; comments spiral into legality, decency, and jokes.
ideal.why_podcast_worthy: Tiny setup, massive comment pile-on—classic quick-hit neighborhood gross-out with legal pedantry.

ideal.summary: Provocative one-liner claiming coyotes are harmless in Seattle; thread devolves into mushrooms jokes, euthanasia hot takes, and fact fights.
ideal.why_podcast_worthy: Bait post that reliably starts a neighborhood flame war—funny meta fodder for a show.
